stories.title: Mozambique: Banning a Film of People Saying They Are Powerless Stresses What They Are Saying
stories.summary: Mozambique: Banning a Film of People Saying They Are Powerless Stresses What They Are Saying 27 November 2026 Mozambique News Reports And Clippings (Milton Keynes, UK) The treason trial of Venancio Mondlane is claiming to ask who is responsible for the violence in the post-election demonstrations. The answer from ordinary people filmed in demonstrations and interviews is in the banned OMR film “Isn’t this our country?” (Nao e nosso pais este aqui?) The 45 minute film is particularly good in recording both the power people felt in the demonstrations, their disempowerment facing the damage done to their lives by mining, and the powerlessness faced by young people with no jobs and no future. The powerlessness was stressed by the 9 October 2024 general elections, with widespread fraud. (I was in Maputo reporting that election for CIP, and the fraud was so great no one knows who actually won.) Ten days later, on 19 October, Elvino Dias, the official lawyer for opposition candidate Venancio Mondlane, was gunned down in Maputo. On 21 October Mondlane held a press conference at the site of the murder, calling for protests, and he and the journalists were teargassed by the police. That propelled the demonstrations, but in protests from 21 to 25 October police killed 24 people.

stories.title: Africa: El Niño Adds New Hunger Hotspots As Conflict Continues to Drive Risk of Famine, Warn FAO and WFP
stories.summary: Africa: El NiÃ±o Adds New Hunger Hotspots As Conflict Continues to Drive Risk of Famine, Warn FAO and WFP 27 November 2026 United Nations World Food Programme (Rome) Rome — Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, parts of Nigeria and Yemen remain hotspots of highest concern with Southern Africa and the Central American Dry Corridor among new additions El Niño has pushed Southern Africa and the Central American Dry Corridor onto the list of hunger hotspots, where acute food insecurity is projected to worsen significantly between December 2026 and May 2027, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) warned today. In their latest Hunger Hotspots report , the agencies also identified a risk of famine in parts of Sudan and South Sudan. The report, released twice a year through the Global Network Against Food Crises, lists 16 hotspots, up from 13 in June. El Niño is a major driver behind three of the four newly identified hotspots: Southern Africa (Eswatini, Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia and Zimbabwe), the Central American Dry Corridor and northeastern Uganda. Chad has been added to the list due to the continued spillover effects of the conflict in neighbouring Sudan.

Lou Osbourn co-founded All Eyes On Wagner, a collective of journalists and cybersecurity analysts. She said the losses prove that Russian fighters are taking part in operations alongside Malian troops and that "Africa remains an area of interest for Moscow". The United Kingdom's The Guardian newspaper - which had access to the leaked records through a media consortium that includes RFI - reported on Tuesday that 349 Russian fighters were killed in Mali between September 2023 and September 2026. It based its tally on death certificates held by Russia's national statistics agency, Rosstat, but said that the real figure was probably higher because deaths can take time to be registered.

stories.summary: Zimbabwe Plans $1.3 Billion Cargo Hub to Boost Exports, Regional Trade The Herald Robert Gabriel Mugabe International Airport 27 November 2026 New Zimbabwe (London) Zimbabwe is banking on a $1.3 billion cargo infrastructure project at Robert Gabriel Mugabe International Airport to expand air freight capacity, improve export logistics and strengthen its position in regional trade, with construction expected to begin in the first quarter of next year, officials have said. Transvaal Africa chief executive Patson Moyo told journalists at a recent press briefing that the project, being undertaken through a public-private partnership with Airports Company of Zimbabwe (ACZ), would include a dedicated cargo runway and 142 specialised warehouses as the country seeks to build capacity for freight handling and logistics. "The Cargo Village will come with a second runway which will mainly focus on cargo movement, and will have 142 specialised warehouses as well as other amenities like an airport hotel, shopping mall, fuel aviation system and a whole lot more," Moyo said. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines The development, known as the Robert Gabriel Mugabe International Airport Cargo Village (RGMIACV), is being implemented through a special purpose vehicle established by ACZ and Transvaal Africa, with the investment expected to be phased from 2027. The project has been allocated about 1,000 hectares at the airport and is expected to incorporate warehousing, cold-chain infrastructure, aviation services and commercial facilities. The proposed expansion comes as exporters face the need for efficient logistics systems to move goods into international markets, particularly perishable commodities that depend on specialised storage, timely handling and reliable air freight connections.

In each case, officials have said the measures are justified under national laws and security provisions. " Cameroon is very sensitive, and it is important that we know when to criticize the government and when not to criticize the government openly," said Ngam Glory Ani Mbom, a citizen of the central African country. She said fear of arrest and violence discourage political participation. "You cannot talk about democracy when opposition supporters cannot freely express their minds to the public," she told DW. For Ndah Grimbald, deputy secretary-general of Cameroon's opposition Social Democratic Front, one of the biggest obstacles is organizing public meetings. "The first major challenge we face as members of the opposition is the non-authorization of public rallies, public meetings," he said, noting that opposition proposals receive little attention in parliament. The combination of challenges has raised questions about whether the government can defend itself against Islamist militant group al-Shabab while managing growing divisions among political factions. stories.title: How a tiny rare frog became an ecological warning sign for Madagascar
stories.summary: The golden mantella frog is an endangered species that only exists only in two or three places in Madagascar. The island is a biodiversity hotspot, but the high rate of deforestation in the country now threatens many endemic species. Photograph: Chris Scarffe/Courtesy of Madagasikara Voakajy View image in fullscreen The golden mantella frog is an endangered species that only exists only in two or three places in Madagascar. The island is a biodiversity hotspot, but the high rate of deforestation in the country now threatens many endemic species. Photograph: Chris Scarffe/Courtesy of Madagasikara Voakajy How a tiny rare frog became an ecological warning sign for Madagascar The golden mantella is said to be found wherever gold is, making its habitat a target for illegal mining, which is destroying fragile ecosystems across the country A s Albert Rakotoarisoa emerges from the forest into a clearing in Mangabe reserve in the east of Madagascar , he sees dozens of holes dug in the marshy ground, a sign that people have been here to search for gold. “I came a couple of weeks ago, and these weren’t here,” he says as he surveys the damage, counting 40 holes. “I’m really disappointed.” Rakotoarisoa, 52, patrols the area regularly on behalf of a local group of volunteers and Madagasikara Voakajy, an organisation that protects the island’s endemic species and their habitats.

Photograph: 2026 Vantor/AP Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel. The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government. Initial reports said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship.

stories.title: Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Bola Tinubu (in red hat) would be 79 at the end of a second term, if he is re-elected By Mansur Abubakar Reporting from Abuja Published 22 November 2026 Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics. At 38, he is among the young people seeking elected office in a country where about 80% of the population is under 40. He hopes his age will stand in his favour as he campaigns for a seat in the state assembly in the northern Kano state in January's general elections. "Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future," Dalhatu tells the BBC. But Nigeria's political history suggests he faces an uphill battle. Since the return to civilian rule in 1999, Goodluck Jonathan has been the youngest person elected president, taking office at the age of 53.

stories.title: ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
stories.summary: Image source, Gallo Images via Getty Images Image caption, The ANC got the most votes overall but lost control in more than half of the councils it won in 2021 Published 21 November 2026 The party that has dominated South Africa for more than 30 years is in a race against time to secure power-sharing deals in most of the country's cities after a massive drop in its support in this month's local elections. The African National Congress (ANC) suffered its worstâ¯result since it came to power in 1994 when South Africa transitioned from the racist apartheid system to democracy. It won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo, down from six in the last elections. It won the most votes in just two of the country's eight cities, compared with six in 2021. At the national level, the ANC is sharing power with its long-time rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA), but while there is still no official announcement, it appears that ANC party officials do not want to replicate this at the local level.
